rules.path_body_equality: Every identifier present in both a route path and request body must match exactly before lookup, claim, replay, or mutation.
rules.operation_payload_digest: For requests containing input, payload_digest is lowercase SHA-256 over canonical JSON of input. For proposal create, correct, reject, and approve it is lowercase SHA-256 over canonical JSON of every request property except contract_name, contract_version, request_id, idempotency_key, payload_digest, and operation_request. Canonical JSON uses UTF-8, sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace, and preserves array order.
rules.content_digests: excerpt_digest, before_digest, after_digest, and terminal_draft_digest are lowercase SHA-256 over the exact UTF-8 text in the paired field after CRLF and CR are normalized to LF. Null content has a null digest.
rules.proposal_digest: For the single ordered change, diff_digest uses the accepted engine exact-diff canonical object: change_id, change_kind, expected_content_digest, record_type, replacement_digest, and subject_id. proposal_payload_digest uses the proposal service canonical object: id, subject, replacement, expected, kind, and record_type. Both use canonical JSON SHA-256; replacement_digest equals after_digest and expected_content_digest equals before_digest.
rules.exact_replay_order: Validate contract version, safe identifiers, path/body equality, canonical payload digest, current consent identity where applicable, and stored receipt binding before head comparison or mutation. Exact replay returns the stored successful response.
rules.consent_gate: Readiness exposes a safe consent_identity_digest over the complete current credential, adapter, endpoint, region, storage, retrieval-policy, and notice identity. Consent input must bind that digest. The server rechecks the current identity before exact replay. Missing or stale explicit consent is HTTP 409 capability_rejected/explicit_consent_required. Provider outage is HTTP 503 provider_unavailable.
rules.ask_start_boundary: Return 202 only after the pinned source envelope and source-set digest are durable and before provider dispatch. Exact replay may return 200 and never dispatch twice.
rules.sse_framing: Each event is framed as id: <sequence>, event: <event_type>, data: <canonical generation_event JSON>, followed by a blank line.
rules.sse_resume: Last-Event-ID and after each name the last observed non-negative sequence. If both are supplied they must match. A value greater than the persisted last sequence is HTTP 409 stream_sequence_conflict. Replay emits only greater sequences in order. Disconnect is not cancellation. A terminal event closes the response.
rules.approval_binding: Validate path/body identity and exact proposal_id, proposal_version, source_revision, base_revision, expected_campaign_head, diff_digest, proposal_payload_digest, and warden_confirmed=true before claim or replay.
rules.approval_equality: operation_request.subject_id equals proposal_id; operation_request.intent_digest equals diff_digest; operation_request.expected_revision equals expected_campaign_head and base_revision; published proposal published_revision_id equals published_revision.revision_id.
rules.proposal_operation_equality: For correction and rejection, operation_request.subject_id equals proposal_id and operation_request.expected_revision equals base_revision. These envelope bindings are validated before receipt replay.
rules.stale_approval: Return HTTP 409 proposal_approval_result with the immutable proposal, outcome conflict, published_revision null, and a sanitized stale_revision error. No partial mutation or implied publication is allowed.
rules.proposal_construction: This slice creates exactly one update. The server loads the selected record from base_revision and binds generation_id, source_revision, source_set_digest, and terminal_draft_digest. It normalizes CRLF and CR to LF in both inputs without trimming or otherwise changing either normalized value. It constructs after_content as the complete normalized existing content + exactly two LF + '## Proposed addition' + exactly two LF + the complete normalized terminal Draft. It adds no trailing LF beyond one already present in the Draft. The browser never constructs or transforms this mutation.
rules.correction: Correction names the same change_id and subject_id and supplies the complete corrected after_content for the one change. It cannot change proposal provenance or widen the change set.
rules.authority: Revision-backed records and non-session Ask sources use preparation, canon, or revealed. Each displayed change includes from_authority and to_authority. They are equal unless the request carries a separate explicit visible authority transition, which this slice does not expose. draft_authority and artifact_kind are separate fields and never source authority values.
rules.public_status_mapping: Internal draft, rejected, conflict, published, and quarantined map to the same public values. Internal approving and approved are not returned as completed HTTP outcomes; reads expose them as draft until publication reconciliation returns published or quarantined.
rules.errors: Standalone diagnostics use only the closed error_response fields. Public errors contain category, code, stage, request_id, and retryable only; they have no free-form message or metadata. The approved stale-head response embeds the same closed error object beside the preserved proposal.
rules.csrf: Every Host/Origin-validated same-origin GET/HEAD returns an installation-specific X-CSRF-Token and a matching drydock_csrf cookie with Path=/, SameSite=Strict, and HttpOnly. Invalid Host/Origin returns the global HTTP 403 closed error_response unsafe_binding/request_binding_rejected for API paths without a token, cookie, or CORS opt-in. Every mutating POST requires both CSRF values to match the server-held secret before request parsing or mutation; missing or stale bindings return the global HTTP 403 closed error_response unsafe_binding/csrf_binding_rejected with no CORS opt-in.
